entries.title: I made Loupe, a free and open-source (MPL-2.0) mail app for Android: Readable mode, search expressions, Sieve rules, OpenPGP/S/MIME, no tracking
entries.text:
Hi! I'm the developer. Loupe is a mail client for Android that tries to be calm for everyday use and powerful when you need it:

- **Readable mode** rebuilds HTML newsletters to fit the phone (original and plain text one tap away)
- **Search language**: `from:alice and (subject:invoice or body:"PO 123")`, results from the phone first, then the server
- **Smart Mailboxes, snooze and Sieve rules** stored on your own mail server
- **Subscriptions**: newsletters by sender with read rates and one-tap unsubscribe
- **OpenPGP** (Autocrypt, Thunderbird-compatible) and **S/MIME**
- IMAP/SMTP and JMAP (Fastmail, Stalwart)

No servers of its own, no analytics, no ads. Free to download (pay what you want, optional). Source: https://github.com/BuenGenio/loupe

Website: https://loupe.mx/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=launch

It's early: nightly builds, one developer. I'd love to hear what's missing or broken.

entries.title: Loupe: a new MPL-2.0 mail client for Android with JMAP, Sieve rules, OpenPGP and S/MIME, and no servers of its own
entries.text:
Loupe is a new open-source mail client for Android (Flutter, MPL-2.0). Things that might interest this sub:

- No telemetry, analytics or crash reporting; no servers of its own
- Encrypted local database (sqlite3mc); remote images blocked by default; tracking redirects unwrapped
- Snooze, Smart Mailboxes and rules live on *your* mail server (a Snoozed folder + keyword, IMAP METADATA, Sieve), so nothing is locked into the app
- OpenPGP with Autocrypt, S/MIME with Android KeyChain certificates
- IMAP/SMTP and JMAP

Builds are signed nightly APKs from GitHub Actions; Obtainium works with the GitHub releases. It isn't on F-Droid.

Source: https://github.com/BuenGenio/loupe · Site: https://loupe.mx/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=launch

Feedback very welcome. I'm the developer.

Your mail server is the source of truth.

Loupe keeps rules as Sieve, snooze as a folder + keyword, and Smart Mailboxes in your own mailbox. Switch phones or clients and nothing is trapped.

entries.title: I built a full mail client in Flutter: 11 packages, an encrypted SQLite store, IMAP + JMAP, pure-Dart S/MIME. Notes on what worked
entries.text:
Loupe is an open-source (MPL-2.0) mail app for Android, written in Flutter. Some notes that might be useful to other Flutter devs:

- **Pub workspace monorepo**: 11 packages with a contracts-only `mail_model` at the bottom, so packages could be built in parallel and tested without a device.
- **Storage**: drift + SQLite FTS5 for search, sqlite3mc for encryption.
- **Search**: one parser produces a syntax tree that compiles to SQL, IMAP SEARCH, Gmail's raw search and JMAP filters; server results are post-filtered with the same matcher.
- **Rendering**: Readable mode rebuilds HTML mail from plain widgets: no web view, no scripts.
- **Crypto**: OpenPGP via dart_pg; S/MIME (CMS, PKCS #12, chain validation) in pure Dart on pointycastle, with Android KeyChain keys used through a small platform channel.
- **Marketing screenshots** are rendered from widget tests with real fonts.

Architecture and build steps: https://loupe.mx/development/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=launch · Source: https://github.com/BuenGenio/loupe

Happy to go deeper on any of it.

Built in public:

11 packages
1,900+ automated tests
0 trackers

Every line of Loupe is on GitHub under the MPL-2.0. Nightly APKs come straight from CI.

entries.title: A mobile mail client that keeps its state on your own server: Loupe (Android, open source, JMAP + Sieve)
entries.text:
If you run your own mail (Stalwart, Dovecot, mailcow…), you may like how Loupe works: it has no cloud of its own, so its state lives on your server.

- **Server rules** compiled to Sieve and uploaded over ManageSieve, or over JMAP (RFC 9661)
- **Snooze** = a `Snoozed` folder + a keyword with the wake-up time (documented convention)
- **Smart Mailboxes** stored as IMAP METADATA, or a message in a `Loupe Settings` folder
- **JMAP** accounts with push, plus plain IMAP/SMTP

The app itself: Android, MPL-2.0, no telemetry, encrypted local store, OpenPGP and S/MIME.

Site: https://loupe.mx/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=launch · Source: https://github.com/BuenGenio/loupe

(Check the sub's rules on new-project posts before this goes up: some days are reserved.)

Many mail apps sync your mailbox through their own servers. It makes push and snooze easy, and it means a third party holds a key to your inbox.

Loupe has no servers. I wrote up how its features work anyway, using open standards on your own mail server, and the honest trade-offs:

How do you snooze mail without a server?

1. Move it to a Snoozed folder on your mail server
2. Add a keyword with the wake-up time
3. Any device that follows the convention wakes it

entries.title: Loupe, an open-source Android mail app with native JMAP and push
entries.text:
For Fastmail users on Android looking for a third-party client: Loupe supports JMAP natively, not just IMAP.

- Sync and search over JMAP, with push via EventSource
- Rules written like searches (run on the phone, or as Sieve on servers that offer it)
- Smart Mailboxes saved in your account so they follow you
- Readable mode, a search language, OpenPGP and S/MIME

It's free, MPL-2.0, and has no servers of its own. Setup: https://loupe.mx/docs/accounts/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=no-cloud

I'm the developer; feedback from Fastmail users especially welcome.

entries.text:
S/MIME in Loupe: certificates installed on the Android device (by your IT department or in Settings) can sign and decrypt without the key ever leaving the keystore. PKCS #12 import, optional passphrases, opt-in OCSP/CRL revocation checks.

https://loupe.mx/docs/encryption/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=encryption

#SMIME #Email #Encryption #FOSS

media.alt: Dark card: 'S/MIME. Use the certificate your company already gave you. Loupe signs and decrypts with certificates installed on your Android device.'

entries.text:
If your organisation issues S/MIME certificates, Loupe can use them on Android: it signs and decrypts with certificates installed in the device's KeyChain, so the private key never leaves the keystore. PKCS #12 import, passphrases and opt-in revocation checks are supported too.

Open source, no servers, no telemetry: https://loupe.mx/docs/encryption/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=encryption
